target.title: feat: add secure read-only MCP server
target.body:
## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default, stateless Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at exact `/mcp`
- expose exactly two read-only tools: cached tweet search and cached thread reads
- bind every response to one server-selected Birdclaw account; exclude DMs, live X access, OpenAI, arbitrary filesystem access, and every mutation path
- isolate the MCP virtual host from the existing UI, static assets, SSR, and write-capable web APIs
- document local clients, Codex configuration, reverse-proxy deployment, and the security model

## Security model

- **Fail closed:** partial or invalid configuration prevents startup; external URLs require HTTPS, loopback URLs may use HTTP, credentials/query/fragment/wrong paths are rejected, and the MCP token must be a strong RFC 6750 bearer value distinct from the web token.
- **Independent request boundary:** exact raw request target, canonical Host, optional exact Origin, loopback socket provenance, bearer auth, duplicate-header rejection, cross-site rejection, and request-smuggling checks happen before MCP dispatch.
- **Reserved virtual host:** canonical and equivalent host forms (case, trailing dot, explicit ports) can reach only `/mcp`; UI, assets, SSR, and `/api/*` remain unreachable even when remote web access is enabled.
- **Read-only storage:** MCP opens an already-initialized current-schema SQLite database in strict read-only mode. It never creates, migrates, imports, syncs, fetches, or writes.
- **Account isolation:** account IDs are literal values, not the UI's `all` sentinel. Search membership, thread ancestors/descendants, collection state, referenced retweets, and relationship IDs are scoped independently so foreign-account data and pointers cannot leak.
- **Bounded work:** 64 KiB request bodies, 30 s deadlines, rate and concurrency limits, 2 MiB serialized results, bounded FTS/account candidates, bounded recursive threads, and lossless `(createdAt, id)` pagination.
- **Prompt-injection posture:** cached social text, names, links, and media are explicitly labeled untrusted data in server instructions and every tool result.

## Validation

- `pnpm run check`
- `pnpm run coverage` — 145 test files, 1,270 tests; 89.15% statements / 80.33% branches / 90.68% lines
- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run pack:smoke` — 126-file tarball, fresh install, real TCP server, official MCP SDK initialize/list/call/close, UI/SSR checks, and graceful SIGTERM
- exact-head GitHub Actions on `1022088` — formatting/lint/types, coverage, build, installed-package smoke, Playwright E2E, and GitGuardian
- source-aware autoreview split across the complete production and test trees — zero actionable findings
- adversarial data testing — cross-account isolation, malformed accounts, strict read-only DB, equal-time cursors, cycles/fanout, snapshot consistency, 2 MiB results, 10k/1k candidate bounds, and 200k sparse collections
- adversarial raw HTTP testing — 114 target-normalization attacks, Host aliases, duplicate auth, absolute/network-path forms, TE+CL, stalled uploads/readers, concurrency recovery, 64 KiB boundary, spoofed forwarding headers, Origin/cookie/web-token separation, and reserved-vhost write-route denial
- source-blind installed-tarball validation from fresh homes — official SDK lifecycle, fail-closed config, byte-for-byte read-only SQLite/WAL/SHM state, stateless sessions, 80 reserved-host surface probes, and regression attacks against every formerly vulnerable Host/path variant

## Compatibility

MCP remains off unless both `BIRDCLAW_MCP_PUBLIC_URL` and `BIRDCLAW_MCP_TOKEN` are configured. Existing local web and CLI behavior is unchanged when MCP is disabled.
